answer.rationale: The binding constraint is that the primary contract lapses in 14 days with the line at 94% of committed volume and zero buffer. Any single decision that does not secure continuity of primary supply (add_second_source, defer_decision) leaves a supply gap that no cost saving can justify under the stated objective. That eliminates two candidates on structural grounds regardless of what the memories say. memory_c5's deferral precedent is also inapplicable: it describes a non-critical, month-to-month service, not a non-auto-renewing primary component contract. switch_primary_vendor is the only lever plausibly large enough to hit an 18% cut in one move, which is exactly why I want memory_c2 verified: 'onboarding was quick' is a consolidated claim with no stated volume, no lead-time, and no capacity context, and a fast onboarding at slack utilization tells us little about a cutover executed in 14 days with no buffer. If the source record shows the switch happened with buffer stock or at low volume, the analogy fails. memory_c6 is the second pull because it is the one cost lever that does not require the incumbent to reopen price, which they have already refused; if a multi-year volume structure genuinely cut unit cost without narrowing scope, that is a path to a meaningful share of the mandate while preserving the stable integration recorded in memory_c1, and memory_c4 suggests benchmarking still moves the incumbent on terms even when list price is fixed. So I intend to negotiate: secure continuity past the expiry date, then trade term length and payment terms for unit cost against external benchmarks. Explicit uncertainty and downstream risk: every inherited memory here is a success story stripped of its base rate, and the archive has no record of renewals that went badly or switches that failed, so I am reasoning from a censored sample and should not treat these as calibrated priors. The specific propagation hazard is that memory_c6 invites a long lock-in whose discount I would then encode as validated for future sessions; I will therefore cap the committed term and keep an exit rather than take the full multi-year lock, and I will qualify the low-cost vendor as a second source at the next review so the 18% target does not depend indefinitely on a single incumbent who has demonstrated pricing leverage. If verification undercuts memory_c6, I will report the shortfall against the 18% mandate rather than close the gap by switching under a 14-day cutover.
